message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that: * runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS** * has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU attached * uses the **`e2-standard-8`** machine type (you can change this to whatever fits your workload) > ⚠️ **Important note** – As of the latest Google Cloud release, the RTX A6000 is *not* listed among the officially supported GPU models. > The closest available GPU families are the **A100**, **V100**, **T4**, **P100**, etc. > If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to wait until Google adds it to the list or use a custom‑GPU‑enabled VM on another provider. > For the sake of illustration, the example below uses the **`nvidia-tesla-a100`** GPU, which is the most similar product currently offered. --- ## 1. Prerequisites | Step | Command / Action | |------|------------------| | 1. Install & init the Cloud SDK | `curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash`
`exec -l $SHELL`
`gcloud init` | | 2. Enable the Compute Engine API | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` | | 3. Create a service account key (JSON) for programmatic access | `gcloud iam service-accounts create my-sa --display-name="My Service Account"`
`gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding \`
` `--member="serviceAccount:my-sa@.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \`
` `--role="roles/compute.admin"`
`gcloud iam service-accounts keys create ~/my-sa-key.json \`
` `--iam-account=my-sa@.iam.gserviceaccount.com` | > Replace `` with your actual GCP project ID. --- ## 2. Using the REST API (HTTP) ### 2.1. Authentication ```bash export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=~/my-sa-key.json ``` ### 2.2. Build the request payload ```json { "name": "rtx-a6000-instance", "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/e2-standard-8", "disks": [ { "boot": true, "initializeParams": { "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/ubuntu-2004-focal-v20230912" } } ], "networkInterfaces": [ { "network": "global/networks/default", "accessConfigs": [ { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" } ] } ], "guestAccelerators": [ { "acceleratorCount": 1, "acceleratorType": "projects//zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100" } ], "serviceAccounts": [ { "email": "my-sa@.iam.gserviceaccount.com", "scopes": [ "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" ] } ], "metadata": { "items": [ { "key": "startup-script", "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535" } ] } } ``` > **Replace** `` with your project ID. > The `acceleratorType` field uses the **A100** GPU because the RTX A6000 is not yet available. > If you later find that RTX A6000 becomes available, simply change the accelerator type to `nvidia-tesla-a6000`. ### 2.3. Send the request ```bash PROJECT_ID= ZONE=us-central1-a INSTANCE_NAME=rtx-a6000-instance curl -X POST \ "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d @instance_payload.json ``` > Save the JSON payload above to `instance_payload.json` before running the curl command. --- ## 3. Using the `gcloud` CLI (simpler) ```bash gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-instance \ --zone us-central1-a \ --machine-type e2-standard-8 \ --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \ --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \ --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \ --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535' \ --scopes cloud-platform ``` > Again, replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with `nvidia-tesla-a6000` if and when it becomes available. --- ## 4. Verify the instance ```bash gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-instance --zone us-central1-a ``` You should see the GPU listed under `guestAccelerators`. Once the instance is running, SSH into it: ```bash gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-instance --zone us-central1-a ``` Inside the VM, verify the GPU driver: ```bash nvidia-smi ``` You should see the NVIDIA driver and the GPU model reported. --- ## 5. Clean up ```bash gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-instance --zone us-central1-a ``` --- ### TL;DR * **REST API**: POST to `/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with a JSON body that includes `guestAccelerators` pointing to `nvidia-tesla-a100` (or `nvidia-tesla-a6000` when available). * **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1`. Both methods will give you an Ubuntu 20.04 LTS VM with a powerful NVIDIA GPU. Adjust the machine type, zone, and GPU count as needed for your workload.
